mechanism_trace.adaptive_D1_program_behavior: Selects python${ENVSOLVE_TARGET_PYTHON}; the same retained program passed Python 3.10 and 3.11 fresh replays.
mechanism_trace.static_D1_program_behavior: Declares ENVSOLVE_TARGET_PYTHON but invokes hard-coded python3.10; D2 therefore observed Python 3.10.13 when Python 3.11 was required.
mechanism_trace.static_D2_repair: A fresh gpt-5.6-sol xhigh Agent replaced the hard-coded interpreter with python${ENVSOLVE_TARGET_PYTHON}, then qualified and Official-passed.

invalid_engineering_attempt.disposition: Excluded from paired outcomes because the declared target input was not supplied consistently across replay paths; all costs remain recorded in the amendment.

scientific_assessment.main_contradiction: The latest static program can remain Official-correct after every episode while forgetting a previously successful deployment condition and requiring repeated strong-Agent repair.
scientific_assessment.strongest_supporting_evidence: On the preregistered D2 return condition, adaptive reused one executable installer with zero model tokens and passed D0, D1, D2, and Official; static failed preflight, spent 656857 input tokens on a new Agent repair, and then Official-passed.
scientific_assessment.strongest_counterevidence_or_alternative: This is one consumed project, one model sample per arm, and one synthetic Python-version reversal. The adaptive D1 prompt may simply have induced parameterization that the equally capable static Agent could produce stochastically; both arms have identical 2/2 Official success.
scientific_assessment.why_not_promote: The pilot establishes feasibility and a within-sequence efficiency advantage, not a general success-rate gain or benchmark-level generalization.
scientific_assessment.why_not_kill: Adaptive met the preregistered retention criterion: it preserved Official success while eliminating the D2 Agent fallback even after charging historical regression replays.
scientific_assessment.next_highest_information_experiment: Preregister a small outcome-blind set of previously consumed projects with naturally distinct deployment conditions, repeat the same static-versus-adaptive sequence, and test whether adaptive increases terminal success or consistently removes fallback calls after all lifecycle costs are charged.
